title: Data protection by design and by default
summary: Controllers must implement appropriate technical and organisational measures, such as pseudonymisation and data minimisation, both when determining the means of processing and during processing, and must ensure by default that only personal data necessary for each purpose are processed.
excerpt: The controller shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures for ensuring that, by default, only personal data which are necessary for each specific purpose of the processing are processed.
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official OJ text (CELEX 32016R0679). Standing note 2026-09-16: the Digital Omnibus on data, COM(2025) 837 (procedure 2025/0360(COD)), is still in ITRE/LIBE committee — its proposed changes to Art. 4(1), Art. 9(2)(k), Art. 33 (96 h via the NIS2 single entry point), Art. 35 (EU-wide DPIA template) and new Arts. 88a/88b are not law and are not recorded here; Arts. 25, 30, 32 and 44-49 are untouched by that proposal.

title: Security of processing
summary: Controllers and processors must implement appropriate technical and organisational security measures for the risk, including where appropriate pseudonymisation and encryption, resilience of systems, restoration of availability and regular testing of effectiveness.
excerpt: Taking into account the state of the art, the costs of implementation and the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risk of varying likelihood and severity for the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller and the processor shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures …
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official OJ text (CELEX 32016R0679). Standing note 2026-09-16: the Digital Omnibus on data, COM(2025) 837 (procedure 2025/0360(COD)), is still in ITRE/LIBE committee — its proposed changes to Art. 4(1), Art. 9(2)(k), Art. 33 (96 h via the NIS2 single entry point), Art. 35 (EU-wide DPIA template) and new Arts. 88a/88b are not law and are not recorded here; Arts. 25, 30, 32 and 44-49 are untouched by that proposal.

title: General principle for transfers
summary: Personal data may be transferred to a third country or international organisation only if the conditions in Chapter V are met, so that the level of protection guaranteed by the Regulation is not undermined.
excerpt: Any transfer of personal data which are undergoing processing or are intended for processing after transfer to a third country or to an international organisation shall take place only if, subject to the other provisions of this Regulation, the conditions laid down in this Chapter are complied with by the controller and processor …
note: Verified 2026-09-10 against the official OJ text (CELEX 32016R0679). Standing note 2026-09-16: the Digital Omnibus on data, COM(2025) 837 (procedure 2025/0360(COD)), is still in ITRE/LIBE committee — its proposed changes to Art. 4(1), Art. 9(2)(k), Art. 33 (96 h via the NIS2 single entry point), Art. 35 (EU-wide DPIA template) and new Arts. 88a/88b are not law and are not recorded here; Arts. 25, 30, 32 and 44-49 are untouched by that proposal.

title: Records of processing activities
summary: Each controller and processor keeps a record of the processing activities under its responsibility, including the purposes, the categories of data subjects, personal data and recipients, transfers to third countries, erasure time limits and a general description of the technical and organisational security measures.
excerpt: Each controller and, where applicable, the controller's representative, shall maintain a record of processing activities under its responsibility.
note: Verified 2026-09-16 against the official OJ text fetched from EUR-Lex (CELEX 32016R0679). title: Security of processing — pseudonymisation and encryption
summary: The first limb of the appropriate security measures names pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data; on a drawing this is the declared encryption of a flow or store and the presence of a masking or pseudonymisation component on the path.
excerpt: the pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data
note: Verified 2026-09-16 against the official OJ text fetched from EUR-Lex (CELEX 32016R0679). Paragraph-level record split out of GDPR:Art32 because (a) and (c) are architectural while (b) and (d) are partly or wholly process. title: Data protection impact assessment
summary: Where a type of processing, in particular using new technologies, is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller carries out an impact assessment before the processing; a systematic and extensive automated evaluation producing legal or similarly significant effects is one of the listed triggers.
excerpt: Where a type of processing in particular using new technologies, and taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of the processing, is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, the controller shall, prior to the processing, carry out an assessment of the impact of the envisaged processing operations on the protection of personal data.
note: Verified 2026-09-16 against the official OJ text fetched from EUR-Lex (CELEX 32016R0679). The architecture supplies the scaffolding of the assessment (processing operations, data flows, recipients, oversight steps); the assessment's conclusion is never a tool output. Standing note 2026-09-16: the Digital Omnibus on data, COM(2025) 837 (procedure 2025/0360(COD)), is still in ITRE/LIBE committee — its proposed changes to Art. 4(1), Art. 9(2)(k), Art. 33 (96 h via the NIS2 single entry point), Art. 35 (EU-wide DPIA template) and new Arts. 88a/88b are not law and are not recorded here; Arts. 25, 30, 32 and 44-49 are untouched by that proposal.

title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
summary: Absent an adequacy decision, a transfer to a third country needs appropriate safeguards — the instruments listed in Art. 46(2), such as standard data protection clauses or binding corporate rules — together with enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies.
excerpt: In the absence of a decision pursuant to Article 45(3), a controller or processor may transfer personal data to a third country or an international organisation only if the controller or processor has provided appropriate safeguards, and on condition that enforceable data subject rights and effective legal remedies for data subjects are available.
note: Verified 2026-09-16 against the official OJ text fetched from EUR-Lex (CELEX 32016R0679). The drawing evidences the transfer itself (region of each node, the flow that crosses it); the safeguard instrument is a contractual fact recorded beside it. title: Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
summary: A data subject has the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces legal effects concerning them or similarly significantly affects them, unless the decision is necessary for a contract, authorised by law with safeguards, or based on explicit consent; in the first and last cases the controller implements safeguards, at least the right to obtain human intervention, to express a point of view and to contest the decision.
note: Tied to the agent's human_in_the_loop[] and human_step in the model: the drawing shows whether a person can intervene, never whether a decision is 'solely automated' in law. title: Territorial scope
summary: The Regulation applies to processing in the context of the activities of an establishment of a controller or processor in the Union, whether or not the processing takes place in the Union (Art. 3(1)); and to processing of personal data of data subjects who are in the Union by a controller or processor not established in the Union, where the processing relates to offering goods or services to them in the Union, irrespective of payment, or to monitoring their behaviour as far as it takes place within the Union (Art. 3(2)).
note: Cited by corpus/applicability.json for GDPR's applies_when (EU establishment, or the gdpr_art3_2 intake fact for a Swiss deployer offering to or monitoring people in the EU); cited side by side with FADP. title: Notification of a personal data breach to the supervisory authority
summary: After a personal data breach the controller notifies the competent supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons; a later notification gives the reasons for the delay. A processor notifies the controller without undue delay. The notification describes the breach, its likely consequences and the measures taken or proposed, and the controller documents every breach (Art. 33(5)).
note: Event-driven duty: its evidence is the declared breach notification path (the architecture's incident_reporting), cited by IRR-005 (the GDPR twin of IRR-001, which cites FADP:2023:Art24 alone; split 2026-10-02 so a finding never cites a regime the architecture does not declare); no cadence entry. The Digital Omnibus proposal COM(2025) 837 would change Art. 33 (96 hours through the NIS2 single entry point); it is not law and is not recorded here.
